findings.finding: The explicitly profiled bullet-flight transport, bounded admission, identity classification, cleanup and stock fallback form an accepted Step 3 foundation.
findings.consequence: Step 3 may close only within the nine selectable-profile boundary.
findings.next: Preserve the exact-profile and fail-closed contracts.

findings.finding: No verified exact-once full-context boundary currently proves committed health and limb writes with all engine modifiers.
findings.consequence: NVO cannot safely replace direct damage.
findings.next: Establish the application and scaling contract before enabling a damage hook.

findings.finding: Contact speed and energy remain diagnostic ranges or unavailable for important paths; the 3U1 world recheck uses a baseline engine segment and pre-movement contacts are unavailable.
findings.consequence: Estimated values cannot be used as authoritative armour or wound inputs.
findings.next: Use explicit validity states in shadow mode and retain engine behavior where the input is not authoritative.

findings.finding: Collision region, ActorHitData region, VATS aim/result and critical semantics do not yet have one tested authority policy.
findings.consequence: Anatomy and armour coverage could be assigned to the wrong body region.
findings.next: Preserve the separate observations and test a policy before damage activation.

findings.finding: The pure AdmissionLedger exists offline, while active hit and impact observations remain bounded diagnostics rather than gameplay state.
findings.consequence: Diagnostic eviction or loss cannot be allowed to change damage outcomes.
findings.next: Create a separate gameplay ledger with explicit lifetime and serialization rules.

findings.finding: Laser, plasma, flame, explosive, thrown, melee and pellet-specific behavior have no active NVO authority adapter.
findings.consequence: The Step 3 closure does not cover those families.
findings.next: Implement and verify one fail-closed family adapter at a time after the shared armour contract.

findings.finding: The capacity test used 127 inert reservations plus one real shot; synchronous per-row logging under locks remains a hot-path concern.
findings.consequence: The current evidence does not establish a universal real-combat performance ceiling.
findings.next: Disable or buffer production logging and measure real concurrent projectiles and multiple actors before activation.

findings.finding: Only nine profiles select automatically; two more are pilot-only and unknown equipment follows the engine path.
findings.consequence: Coverage is intentionally partial but fails closed.
findings.next: Expand through authored compatibility profiles rather than heuristic ownership.

findings.finding: Brahmin Baron registrations are retired for the current compiled records and tested new-game/reload path; migration from older saves is unverified.
findings.consequence: New-game work may proceed, while old-save support needs an explicit policy.
findings.next: Decide whether to migrate or declare pre-retirement saves unsupported before release.

findings.finding: The accepted NVO record state is RD.esm-free and startup ownership no longer requires RD.
findings.consequence: RD is not a blocker for the next combat packet.
findings.next: Keep the RD-free record check in future release validation.

findings.finding: Existing notices are retained, but the archived permission evidence does not settle the redistribution scope of copied BallistX numeric drag tables.
findings.consequence: The technical closure does not establish a broad combined-distribution license claim.
findings.next: Archive applicable permission text or replace or separate the disputed numeric data before public redistribution claims.
